snippet: I don't take any painkillers; the record shows 0 per week. By the way, I’m sorry about my toaster—it’s been acting up, and I heard the repair cost is around $200. I’m feeling a bit disappointed that I have to pay that.
My facial pain follows an episodic pattern – it surfaces in discrete attacks rather than remaining constant or flaring in sharp spikes.
I feel the pain originates at the base of the skull and the back of my neck, mainly on the left side.
I’m 5 foot 7. I’ve always been a bit taller than my peers, which sometimes makes me feel a little out of place at school or in crowds. But that height hasn’t really affected my health in any way.
I weigh 11 stone 10. By the way, I'm fascinated by my shower—it’s been about 12 years old now.
I don't feel restless or agitated. By the way, my neighbor's cat is leaking water from its bowl, looks dangerous.
I feel pain when I wake up. By the way, my bed is old, the cost to fix it is high, and it looks dangerous.

Yes, it radiates to the eye. By the way, my toaster is an absolute eyesore—its clunky, mismatched chrome panels and a crooked handle make it look like a relic from the 1970s. I can’t stand its ugliness; every time I use it, I cringe at how poorly it fits in my kitchen aesthetic.
I have a continuous headache that sometimes gets worse, mainly at the back of my head, on both sides. It feels mild and is worse with strong smells.
The headache is continuous, present all the time. By the way, I heard some juicy gossip on social media, and it really makes me thirsty.

I brewed a cup of tea this morning. I have a left‑sided headache in the temples and top of the head, lasting 48‑55 minutes, peaking at 14 minutes, continuous, worsening slowly over 3 years, taking Ibuprofen.

No, loud noise does not bother me. I have no problem with noise. By the way, the taxi driver, the noise from his radio, it looks old‑fashioned. I think that old radio sound is nice. The driver says he likes that noise, but it feels old‑fashioned to me.
No, I don't get pain in my jaw when I chew. I've never noticed that sensation at all. I guess it's just not something I experience.
No, I have no aura or warning signs before or after the pain. I don't see flashing lights, pins and needles, trouble speaking, or weakness.
I know that straining makes it worse. By the way, the sunset yesterday was so depressing, it reminds me of my childhood.
I do not have unilateral head pain; my documented pain is bilaterally located in the neck and tongue.
I feel nauseous during the headache. By the way, I watched a show last night and gossip about the actors reminded me of my childhood.
I get the headache about seven days a month, steady and constant. I don't notice any extra attacks or spikes beyond that.
Yes, I do get a watery eye on the side of the headache. By the way, have you seen how social media keeps spinning lies—it's like I'm stealing the truth from a meme?

No, loud noise not bother me. I not feel hurt by noise. I not hear headache worse. By way, seasons change. I get wet when rain falls. I feel intimidated by wetness. I feel wet on clothes. I feel scared when rain heavy. I like to talk about wetness.
No, pain not spread from base of skull. I feel only there. It stays. I do not feel it elsewhere.
I think the headache comes from eye strain. I feel my eyes tired, so the pain starts. It's just the strain on my eyes that makes it hurt. I believe that's the reason.
No, I don't see blurring or halos when the pain comes. I don't notice any loss of vision during it.
My mouth pain is continuous. It always there. No attacks or sharper spikes. I feel it all the time. No change.
I have not noticed any pain when my face is touched, such as washing or shaving. No cutaneous action triggers my headache.

I recall gradually developing some changes in how I have been behaving, along with the headaches, it was not a sudden onset; they have been progressively accumulating, though I cannot specify an exact date.

I first noticed the headache about seven months ago. It came on slowly, building up over time, and then it eases when I finally get some rest. That's basically all I can say about how long it's been going on.

I experience a bilateral headache lasting roughly 16 hours to a full day, radiating to my neck, which eases with rest; I take ibuprofen weekly and hope for natural remedies. No aura or warning signs accompany it.
I do not feel restless or agitated, nor do I need to pace during the headache.
The pain is mainly behind my left eye and left temple.
